messages.text: South Africa win decider over Aussies to take series and go top of Test rankings

metadata.summary: South Africa thumped Australia by 176 runs at Newlands as the hosts' bowling attack produced fireworks to clinch a 2-1 victory in the three-match series between the countries and propel the Proteas to the top of the ICC Men's Test Team Rankings.
metadata.content: South Africa vs Australia, third Test: Proteas win Newlands decider to take series and soar to top of Test rankings | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content South Africa vs Australia, third Test: Proteas win Newlands decider to take series and soar to top of Test rankings South Africa won third Test at Newlands by 176 runs to take series 2-1 and replace Australia at top of Test rankings; Kagiso Rabada took two wickets in the first over of the chase and his 350th in Tests three wickets later, before Simon Harmer racked up six on the day Stuart Hodge @Hodgeythehack Saturday 31 October 2026 14:46, UK Image: South Africa deservedly took victory in the third Test to claim the series win over Australia (AP Photo/Halden Krog) South Africa thumped Australia by 176 runs at Newlands as the hosts' bowling attack produced fireworks to clinch a 2-1 victory in the three-match series between the countries and propel the Proteas to the top of the ICC Men's Test Team Rankings. This wasn't a chase that drifted away; it was snatched from Australia early on. Kagiso Rabada ripped through it in the first over and spinner Simon Harmer took a career-best 6-16 to destroy any hopes of a comeback. Set a target of 288 for victory, the tourists were bowled out for 111 as South Africa leapfrogged them to go top of the Test world rankings for the first time since January 2016. Credit: Netflix Fallon Sherrock says she has "overcome the hate" after beating Luke Littler to win the second-biggest prize in darts history. The 32-year-old was crowned champion of Netflix's 'Beat Luke Littler' on Friday night after she overcame the double world champion in a one-off leg of 501 to claim a mammoth £501,000 prize. Only Littler himself has taken more from a single prize pot, the £1million he collected for his second World Championship in January. metadata.content: Maybank Championship: Miyu Yamashita in command as Charley Hull and Lottie Woad fall away in Kuala Lumpur | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Maybank Championship: Miyu Yamashita in command as Charley Hull and Lottie Woad fall away in Kuala Lumpur Leader Miyu Yamashita is aiming to defend a title for the first time in Malaysia; Yan Liu was the star of the field, shooting 63 on Saturday; Lottie Woad shot 65 but is 10 shots back; watch the final round from 1.30am on Sunday on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Mix Stuart Hodge @Hodgeythehack Saturday 31 October 2026 09:13, UK Image: Miyu Yamashita of Japan reacts after teeing off on the third hole at the Maybank Championship (AP Photo/Vincent Thian) Defending champion Miyu Yamashita carries a two-stroke lead into Sunday's final round of the LPGA Tour's Maybank Championship after shooting a five-under 67 on Saturday. The 2025 Women's British Open winner and second-round leader had a 54-hole total of 198 to sit 18-under par overall at the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club course. "It was a very nice round today as well," said Yamashita. "I had a few tricky situations during the round, but I managed to get through them and finish without dropping a shot, so I'm really pleased with that.
